question: Which Five Year Plan Focused on rapid industrialization of heavy & basic industries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 3, which is the 2nd Five Year Plan.**
 
• ** The 2nd Five Year Plan was initiated in 1956 and continued till 1961.**
 
• The primary objective of the plan was to **promote heavy and basic industries, such as steel, coal, power, and machine tools, to boost the country's industrial growth.**
 
• The plan aimed to achieve an annual growth rate of** 7% in industrial production.** It also focused on increasing agricultural production and improving the standard of living of the people.
 
• The plan's success was marred by several factors, such as poor implementation, inadequate infrastructure, and the Indo-China war, which disrupted the economy.
 
• The 2nd Five Year Plan laid the foundation for India's industrialization and set the tone for subsequent plans.
 
• It emphasized the importance of **self-reliance and the need to reduce dependence on foreign aid and technology.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****The 1st Five Year Plan** was launched in** 1951** and focused on agriculture, rural development, and community development. It aimed to achieve an annual growth rate of 2.1%, but it achieved a growth rate of 3.6%.
 
• **The 3rd Five Year Plan **was initiated in** 1961 and continued till 1966**.
 
 
• It aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.6% in industrial production and focused on** reducing poverty and unemployment.**
 
 
 
• ** The 4th Five Year Plan** was launched in 1969 and continued** till 1974**.
 
 
• It aimed to achieve an annual growth rate of 5.7% and focused on achieving self-sufficiency in food production, promoting exports, and reducing regional imbalances.
 
 
 
• **The 5th Five Year Plan** was initiated in **1974 and continued till 1979.**
 
 
• **​** It aimed to achieve an annual growth rate of 5.5% and focused on reducing poverty, improving the standard of living, and promoting rural development.
